Hi Alex / Sarah —

Great conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the Horizon POC:

1) Environment details (ACTION: Horizon)
   - Which network pattern will you use for the POC? (VPC endpoint/private link vs public egress). Please confirm VPC CIDR and whether you have a NAT gateway or egress appliance.

2) IP allowlist / firewall (ACTION: Horizon)
   - We can provide a small set of stable IP ranges for initial allowlisting; long-term we recommend a VPC endpoint or PrivateLink. If you must use IP allowlists, please share the primary firewall point-of-contact.

3) mTLS & certs (ACTION: Redwood / Horizon)
   - Clarify whether your network team can accept outbound mTLS or you prefer client cert auth. We'll outline both flows below in our tech note.

4) SDK & auth (ACTION: Redwood / Horizon)
   - We'll ship an SDK quickstart for your devs that supports API key auth and optional mTLS. If you want token-based scoped credentials for shorter lived access, let us know.

5) Structured output & tool-calling (ACTION: Redwood)
   - We demonstrated function-style structured outputs on the call. We'll provide two example schemas for your reranker and a sample embedding pipeline.

6) Next technical workshop (ACTION: schedule)
   - Proposed: Tue 2027-10-12 10:00 PT (network + app owners + Redwood infra). Please confirm.

Attached: onramp_connectivity_checklist.pdf — a one-page checklist your networking team can use.

If you can reply with the firewall contact and whether you prefer a PrivateLink vs IP allowlist for the POC, we’ll prepare the technical doc for the workshop.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Alex / Sarah —

Thanks for the quick answers. I'm Karthik from the infra team; below are concrete notes you can share with your networking/security folks. I'll join the workshop and bring config examples.

Network & Egress options - Option A: VPC endpoint (recommended long-term)
   - AWS PrivateLink / ALB endpoint is the preferred pattern. Traffic to Redwood stays inside AWS and you avoid public IP allowlists.
   - DNS: configure a private hosted zone with a CNAME pointing the service name we provide to the PrivateLink endpoint. If you run split-horizon DNS, make sure internal resolver returns the private IPs.
- Option B: Controlled public egress (POC)
   - We'll provide a stable set of egress IPs you can allowlist. These are intended for short-term POCs only. Expect 2–4 IP ranges per region.

mTLS & Certificates - We support mutual TLS for client authentication. Two flows:
   1) Client certs — you generate a CSR and private key; either upload the public cert to our Console (we install the cert for you) or we can accept JKS/PEM bundles through our secure intake form.
   2) Token-based + mTLS for transport — if you want short-lived tokens but also want TLS-level client auth, we can combine both (client cert termination at edge, token used for per-request auth).
- Rotation: we recommend monthly rotation for POC -> quarterly for production. We can automate rotation via our Console API and provide a webhook to notify your KMS.

DNS / Name resolution - Use a friendly internal hostname (api-redwood.horizon.internal) and point it to the PrivateLink. For public egress, allowlist IP ranges and use standard public DNS.

SDK & Auth
- SDKs: official SDKs support API keys and mTLS sockets. For server-side workloads, prefer scoped API keys with expiration. For client-side, use a short-lived token broker pattern (we can provide a token minting endpoint).

Structured output & tool-calling
- We recommend language-model function-calling for structured outputs. Two best practices:
   - Provide a strict JSON schema for the model to follow (we'll include examples).
   - Add a deterministic post-processor that validates schema and rejects unexpected fields.

Embeddings & Reranker guidance
- Embedding model: we recommend the redwood-embedding-2 (i.e., 1536d) family for semantic search at your scale.
- Indexing: use batch embedding with parallel workers and store vectors in your vector DB (Pinecone).
- Reranker: run a lightweight cross-encoder on the top-K candidates (K=20) to reduce calls to the large generator. This balances relevance and per-query cost.
- Caching: prefix-level KV cache for repeated prompts (session or conversation id) reduces token usage.

Attachments & links
- I've attached our private connectivity guide with sample configs: redwood_private_connectivity_guide.pdf
- Quick config snippets I'll paste in the workshop.

Next steps
- I'll prepare a short network checklist + sample Terraform for PrivateLink before the 10/12 workshop.
- Action: Sarah to confirm whether POC will proceed with public egress allowlist or PrivateLink.

Thanks — I'll be on the 10/12 call.

—Karthik
